blockers.title: An empty, unaudited role-applicability factor can still erase a comparison-basis component from G16
blockers.counterexample: Let B be a comparison-basis component identity with a valid nonempty platform set. D-002/DR-118 supply the product role list {TypeScript}, but the subject never records or validates the relation that says which product-selected roles are 'applicable to that identity'. A fixture builder assigns B an empty applicable-role set before hostile mutation. The members product for B is then B × empty-set × platforms(B) × changeClasses = empty-set. No B cell exists, so changes, missing declarations, missing owners, and dependency effects for B are never exercised. The basis digest faithfully commits to the incomplete basis, omission is not an omission inside that basis, and nonShrinkLaw cannot preserve a cell that was never admitted.
blockers.measurement: Role applicability occurs only in fixtureDomainBasis prose: members filters on it, nonShrinkLaw protects alteration after cells exist, and missingMetadata merely says it is product-selected from DR-118. There is no component-to-role applicability object, digest/input pin, schema, nonempty/completeness law, roleless sentinel, C-MISSING-ROLE-APPLICABILITY class, or typed outcome for an initially missing/empty relation. The permitted D-002/DR-118 bytes select the TypeScript role list and its acceptance matrix; they do not supply a closed per-component applicability map in this artifact.
blockers.risk: A harness can qualify an incomplete component/language/platform corpus while never testing an affected component lane, violating DR-G16's no-waiver rule. Freezing and hashing a self-selected empty factor prevents mutation-time shrinkage but does not prove the starting basis complete.
blockers.suggestedFix: Add a custodied, digest-bound component-to-role applicability basis sourced from DR-118, with a MUST-nonempty rule for every comparison-basis component identity or an explicit roleless/N-A sentinel cell. Missing, empty, conflicting, or out-of-list applicability must retain named cells and force REFUSE/NON-PASS. Include that relation in fixtureDomainBasis validation so its digest cannot bless an empty-factor omission.

shouldFix.title: The missing-platform negative has neither a closed cold-start cell shape nor a selector input path
shouldFix.counterexample: Delete the platform set from an otherwise valid component manifest. The ownership/dependency/change-set inputs named by the selector still resolve the changed manifest unit to that component, so the algorithm selects its lane with ambiguity=none. fixtureDomainBasis says the harness may emit explicit NON-PASS, but G16-3 instead requires selectorDecision.ambiguity=refuse-only. Producing that selector value requires inspecting platform metadata that is absent from the selector's classifier, completeness roster, explanations, and inputsDigest. Conversely, for an identity that never had a validated platform set, members has an empty platform factor and missingMetadata asks for named C-MISSING-PLATFORM-METADATA cells without defining any platform coordinate or explicit sentinel set for those cells.
shouldFix.measurement: The entire selector subtree contains no fixtureDomainBasis, platform-metadata, or platform-set input. It names only ownership-record bytes, DR-103 dependency edges, changeSetDigest, and ambiguityPolicy. The new G16 class nevertheless asserts a selector-level REFUSE-only outcome for platform metadata. The safe intent is clear, but the dataflow and cold-start cell shape are not.
shouldFix.risk: Two conforming readings diverge: one follows the selector and emits a selected-lane NON-PASS, while the other adds an uncustodied manifest-platform input to synthesize selector refusal. The cold-start case also lacks a portable four-dimensional cell representation. Both are fail-safe, so this is SHOULD-FIX rather than a second blocker.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Choose one layer. Either add the validated platform set and fixtureDomainBasis digest to the selector's closed inputs, classification step, explanation, and inputsDigest; or remove C-MISSING-PLATFORM-METADATA from selector ambiguity and require a selected component-lane/harness NON-PASS bound to the basis digest. For never-valid sets, enumerate concrete D-002 platform cells or define an explicit platform=MISSING sentinel and its result schema.

shouldFix.title: The deferred Windows slot has no lawful success-neutral disposition
shouldFix.counterexample: At the D-002 preview scope, Windows is intentionally deferred. DEF-WIN requires a 'blocked-on-ride / preview-not-required cell'. G16-4 says blocked-on-ride and INACTIVE ride cells are NON-PASS and prevent G16 qualification, while resultSuccessVersusSlotCompleteness says blocked substitution is lawful only for SL-5 and SL-6. DEF-WIN is a platform slot, not either shared lane. Thus honoring DEF-WIN blocks G16 indefinitely; treating it as success violates both success clauses.
shouldFix.measurement: The corpus correctly prevents silent deletion of Windows, but it never defines a success-neutral deferred-platform standing or exempts the explicitly preview-not-required DEF-WIN slot from the broad blocked-cell NON-PASS rule. The field called owner is also D-002, an authority/decision rather than a responsible actor, but the outcome contradiction is the material issue.
shouldFix.risk: The preview harness is either unqualifiable until the deferred platform enters or must waive an explicit NON-PASS rule. This is an over-strict/ambiguous acceptance oracle rather than unsafe under-selection, so it is SHOULD-FIX.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Give deferred role/platform slots a distinct explicit disposition such as DEFERRED-OUT-OF-PREVIEW-DOMAIN that is slot-complete and qualification-neutral, with a responsible owner and reason, and state that it is not blocked-on-ride/INACTIVE. Alternatively state that the slot is NON-PASS and that G16 intentionally waits for Windows, if that is the product decision.
